history.heading: Between the Maghreb and the Sahel
paragraphs: Mauritania, largely covered by the Sahara Desert, was greener in prehistoric times, as rock art shows. Amazigh (Berber) peoples and Soninke farmers lived there; Koumbi Saleh, in southern Mauritania, is thought to have been the capital of the Ghana Empire.

In the 11th century the Almoravid movement, which arose among Sanhaja Berbers in the region, conquered Morocco and Muslim Spain. Arab tribes, the Beni Hassan, migrated into the area from the 14th century, and Arab-Berber Moorish society formed. Desert towns such as Chinguetti and Ouadane became centres of trade and Islamic scholarship and are UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

history.heading: Colony and independence
paragraphs: France colonised Mauritania in the early 20th century as part of French West Africa. It became independent on 28 November 1960 under Moktar Ould Daddah. Mauritania fought the Polisario Front after dividing Western Sahara with Morocco in 1975, then withdrew in 1979.

Military coups occurred in 1978, 1984, 2005 and 2008. Ethnic tensions led to violence and expulsions of Black Mauritanians in 1989–91. In 2019 the country saw its first peaceful transfer of power between elected presidents, and Mohamed Ould Ghazouani was re-elected in 2024.

culture.heading: Peoples and traditions
paragraphs: Mauritania's population includes Arab-Berber Moors (Bidhan), Haratin (descendants of enslaved people) and Black African groups such as the Fula, Soninke and Wolof. Arabic is the official language, and Hassaniya Arabic is widely spoken. Almost all are Sunni Muslim, and Mauritania is an Islamic Republic.
Nomadic traditions, tea ceremonies and poetry are important. Griot musicians perform with the tidinit lute and ardin harp.

politics.heading: Islamic Republic
paragraphs: Mauritania is a presidential republic. It has been relatively stable compared with its Sahel neighbours and has avoided major jihadist attacks since 2011. Slavery was the last in the world to be officially abolished, in 1981, and criminalised in 2007, but discrimination against the Haratin persists.

economy.heading: Mining, fishing and gas
paragraphs: Iron ore, carried by one of the world's longest trains, gold and copper are the main exports. Mauritania's waters are among the richest fishing grounds in the world. Offshore gas production began in 2025 from a field shared with Senegal, and the country has potential for green hydrogen.
Most people depend on herding and farming, and poverty is widespread. The currency is the ouguiya.
